title: Cost Engineering: Program roadmap and initiative tracker for batching/caching/quantization
creator: Leah Park
description: Program-level ticket to coordinate the cross-functional roadmap and OKR tracking for Redwood's cost optimization programs focused on batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization. Goal: reduce per-token inference cost by 20% for typical web-scale workloads while preserving >=99.5% of current quality SLA and maintaining p99 latency SLOs. This ticket captures milestones, success metrics, rollout strategy, risks and trade-offs, and links to design/engineering artifacts for quarterly PM/ENG syncs.
milestones: Design & safety review: API/SDK controls and opt-in flags (Feb-Mar)
Engineering prototype: batching and prefix cache alpha (Mar-Apr)
Full rollout & postmortem: cost savings report and OKR assessment (Jun)
metrics: Primary KPI: aggregate per-token unit cost change (target -20% vs baseline 2026-01)
Quality guardrail: eval set pass-rate >= 99.5% relative to baseline generation on holdout prompts
Latency guardrail: p99 end-to-end latency not increased by more than 10% for interactive tier
Operational KPI: cache hit rate for prefix caching (> 40% target for web workloads)
Deployment KPI: percent of traffic on optimized path (50% canary -> 100% rollout)
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end integration of batching + prefix caching + recommended quantization profiles in infra repo; 2) End-to-end dashboards show >=20% unit cost reduction on representative tenant group without violating quality/latency guardrails; 3) Runbook and automatic fallback policies in place; 4) PM sign-off on OKR metrics and rollout plan
progress_updates: 2026-01-21: Kickoff with Eng/Research/Console. Agreed to split work across three streams (batching, caching, quantization). Set baseline cost and quality metrics.
2026-02-05: Profiling complete — top 10 customers contribute 65% of peak tail tokens; identified workload shapes amenable to batching and prefix reuse.
2026-02-22: Research delivered quantization regression matrix (8-bit QAT vs post-training static). Initial experiments show quality delta concentrated on long-context summarization tasks.
2026-03-03: Design review: console UX for opt-in toggles and rollout visibility approved with minor copy changes (see design doc).
2026-03-12: Eng prototype for continuous batching landed in feature branch; observed 12% cost reduction in microbenchmarks. Next: integrate prefix cache and run closed-canary.
decisions: Prioritize prefix/KV caching and continuous batching before aggressive quantization to avoid early quality regressions for customers.
Expose conservative quantization profiles as opt-in per model initially; rollback route must be automated via routing policies.
Use tenant-level canary traffic pins for initial rollout to isolate customer risk.
tradeoffs: Aggressive quantization provides larger cost wins but increases risk of semantic regressions — mitigated by staged rollout and eval-driven gating.
Larger batch sizes reduce cost but increase tail latency variability; chosen strategy is adaptive batching with latency SLO-aware caps.
Caching improves per-token cost significantly for repeat prefixes but adds cache invalidation complexity for private deployments.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: quality regressions post-quantization. Mitigation: automated eval harness with representative prompt suites and immediate rollout rollback on metric regression. Risk: increased p99 latency from batching. Mitigation: adaptive batching with p99 monitors and emergency bypass. Risk: cache privacy/compliance in Private deployments. Mitigation: allow per-tenant opt-out and enforce encryption/KMS for cached entries.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha runs on synthetic tenants (2 weeks). 2) Closed canary to 5% traffic for low-risk tenants (3 weeks) with daily quality gating. 3) Expanded canary to 50% with staggered tenant cohorts (2 weeks). 4) Full rollout after 2 successful weeks and PM/Eng sign-off. Include automatic fallback to pre-optimization routes on any violating signal.
open_questions: What is the minimum cache TTL we can use without violating PII retention policies for Private deployments? (Sec to advise)
Which customer cohorts should be excluded from early quantization canaries (enterprise regulated workloads)?
Do we surface per-request 'cost saving' metadata to customers or keep it internal?
next_steps: 1) Eng to complete prefix cache integration and expose telemetry hooks (ETA 2026-03-26). 2) Research to produce the final quantization profile matrix and regression test suite (ETA 2026-04-09). 3) PM to coordinate a legal/privacy review for cache TTLs and write customer communication templates.
notes: Design feedback requested: include contextual help in Console explaining trade-offs between cost and quality.
Action item: Solutions Eng to compile list of 10 pilot customers for closed canary by 2026-03-19.
Reminder: align rollout dates with Dedicated customers' maintenance windows to minimize disruption.
